clue.text: Note grooves encircling a rotating planet

indicators.note: something rotating turns round, so the whole assembled string is read backwards
the grooves go round the next piece, so it sits inside them

parts.note: ruts are grooves worn into a track

explanation.surface: An astronomer describes rings or grooves circling a spinning planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encircling' puts A inside RUTS to give RUTAS; with N in front that is NRUTAS, and 'rotating' turns the lot round.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixth planet from the Sun, famous for its rings, is a straightforward example of a planet.

clue.text: Glum single bloke is disheartened

parts.note: sole means only or single, as in the sole survivor

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the word for bloke is removed

parts.note: a bloke is a man, in British slang

explanation.surface: An unhappy single man feeling downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' means losing the heart, the middle letter, here A.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a grave, serious, unsmiling manner, so they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Bottom of lost, powerless lackey getting hit for so long

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter
P is the abbreviation for power, so without power the P is dropped

parts.note: a poodle is a servile follower, as in a politician being someone's poodle
to pip is to hit with a small shot

explanation.surface: Someone at the bottom of the losers, a feeble lackey, gets hit and says goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom of' gives T; 'powerless' drops P from POODLE to leave OODLE. TOODLE-PIP is dated British slang for goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British farewells, the kind of thing said on parting.

clue.text: Runs daughter in car somewhere in Wales

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: the daughter is placed inside the word for the car

parts.note: a Honda is a make of car

explanation.surface: Someone drives a daughter somewhere in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts D inside HONDA, giving HONDDA, after R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhondda is a valley and former coal-mining district in South Wales, so it is a place in that country.

clue.text: Old boat worker briefly brought back shells round Channel Island

indicators.note: to shell something is to enclose it, so the reversed letters go round the next piece
brought back means the shortened word is read in reverse
a word cut short loses its last letter

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in a farm hand
O is round in shape
Sark is one of the Channel Islands, between England and France

explanation.surface: A worker on an old boat collects shells from round one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shells' is a verb here: the reversed, shortened worker encloses O. Sark is a small Channel Island.
explanation.definitionFit: The vessel built by Noah in Genesis to survive the Flood is about as old a boat as there is.

clue.text: On which late correspondents may connect committees supporting European agreements

definitions.text: On which late correspondents may connect

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word sits beneath, so it comes second

parts.note: oui and ja are the French and German words for yes
boards are committees of directors or governors

explanation.surface: Committees back European agreements, sounding like Brussels bureaucracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late correspondents' are the dead, who at a seance supposedly spell out messages on the lettered board.
explanation.definitionFit: These lettered boards are used at seances to contact the dead, so the departed may get in touch through them.

clue.text: Husband regularly heard quote about apostate

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word heard gives its even letters
about here means turned round, so the word for quote is read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A husband keeps hearing his wife quote things against a renegade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes ER from hEaRd; 'about' turns CITE into ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abandons or dissents from orthodox belief can be called either term, so they are near synonyms.

clue.text: Fit to hold boxer's last fight

indicators.note: the word for fit holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: an ague is a fit of fever with shivering

indicators.note: the last letter of boxer is taken

explanation.surface: A fit boxer gets ready to hold his own in the final fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like an adjective for the boxer but is a noun: a fever fit, AGUE, which 'to hold' wraps round R.
explanation.definitionFit: To fight can mean to quarrel with words, a dispute between people, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Capital port that could be excellent if the top 50% is saved for later?

indicators.text: if the top 50% is saved for later
indicators.note: in a down clue the top half of the word comes first, and saving it for later moves those letters to the end

parts.note: stonking is British slang for excellent or tremendous

explanation.surface: A capital port that could be superb if the top half were kept back.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the first four letters, STON, of STONKING to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingston is the capital of Jamaica and a major harbour city, so it is both capital and port.

clue.text: Consider stupid person across floor

indicators.note: the word for stupid person stretches across the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a loon is a fool or silly person
to floor an opponent in boxing is to KO, knock them out

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about a fool sprawled across the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: To floor a boxer is to knock them out, abbreviated KO.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard someone in a particular way is to consider them so, as in viewing him as a friend.

clue.text: Elementary matter of changing ringtone

indicators.note: changing the letters of the word ringtone rearranges them

explanation.surface: The basic question of changing your phone's ringtone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elementary' looks like simple, but here it means relating to a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a chemical element, a gas making up most of the air, so it is matter that is an element.

clue.text: Memory initially affected after air stopped short, causing OTT behaviour

indicators.note: after says the word for memory follows the shortened tune
cut short means the last letter is lost

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody
RAM is random-access computer memory

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of affected is taken

explanation.surface: A memory affected after someone's air supply was cut off, prompting over-the-top behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' is a tune, not breath. OTT means over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Exaggerated, overwrought conduct is described as theatrical in the manner of a sensational stage play, so the sense fits.

clue.text: Youth beginning to arrange deal caught in a meltdown

indicators.note: the beginning of the word arrange is its first letter

parts.note: to dole out is to deal out

indicators.note: the abbreviation for caught goes inside the word for a meltdown

parts.note: making a scene is having a tantrum or meltdown
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A young person starts to arrange a deal, caught up in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C inside SCENE to give SCENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The period of being young, between childhood and adulthood, is the teenage years, so youth names it.

clue.text: Force unopened lock

indicators.note: unopened means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: stress is force exerted on something

explanation.surface: Someone forces a lock that has not been opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' looks like a door lock but is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A curl or length of hair is called a lock, and this word is the poetic equivalent.

clue.text: Quietly contrive to agree over key arrangement?

parts.note: piano is the musical direction for playing quietly
to concert is to arrange something by mutual agreement
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone quietly tries to agree on a key arrangement in a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key arrangement' points to piano keys and musical arrangement rather than a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition for keyboard soloist and orchestra is a musical arrangement featuring keys, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Sort of film adult in bar having to shift when one enters

indicators.note: the adult letter goes inside the word for bar

parts.note: a rod is a bar
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: the numeral enters, going inside, the word for shift

parts.note: to move is to shift
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An adult in a bar has to move when someone else comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives ROAD; 'enters' gives MOVIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre of film built around a journey, such as Easy Rider, is one sort of film.

clue.text: Weeds grass outside, say, Oxford emporium

indicators.note: the word for grass goes outside the word for weeds

parts.note: to grass is British slang for inform on, and so is to shop
to weed with a hoe is to hoe, so weeds means hoes

explanation.surface: A gardener weeds the grass outside an Oxford store.
explanation.walkthrough: An Oxford is a lace-up shoe, not the city; 'grass' is British slang for inform on.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a style of lace-up footwear, so a store selling it is the kind of emporium meant.

clue.text: It affects view from new Tipperary home

indicators.note: new means the letters of the words Tipperary home are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: Something affecting the view from a new home in Tipperary, the Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'view' suggests scenery but means eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-sightedness is a condition of the eye that impairs near vision, so it affects how one sees.

clue.text: Mineral water at last needed by a cracking composer

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of water
the letter a cracks the composer's name, going inside it

parts.note: Edward Elgar was an English composer

explanation.surface: A mineral water is finally needed by a composer hard at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' puts A inside ELGAR, giving EALGAR, after R.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic sulphide, an orange-red ore, is a mineral, so it is one example.

clue.text: Work up appetite, primarily to eat fast food in Italy

indicators.note: the outer letters eat the fast, taking it inside
in a down clue up means the letters read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: OP is the abbreviation for opus, a work

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of appetite

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: Someone works up an appetite, mainly to eat fast food in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast food' is a red herring: 'fast' is the Lenten fast, eaten by the surrounding letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornmeal porridge or cake is a staple dish of northern Italy, so it is Italian food.

clue.text: Stigma surrounding large old despot

indicators.note: the word for stigma surrounds the letter for large

parts.note: a stain on one's reputation is a stigma
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A shameful stigma surrounds a big old tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts L inside STAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet leader Joseph was a notorious dictator of the last century, an example of an old tyrant.

clue.text: More contributors to sex trade?

indicators.note: the letters contributing to the words sex trade form the answer within them

explanation.surface: More people taking part in the sex industry?
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is the definition and 'contributors to' the hidden-word signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional means more, as in an additional portion, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Bone in good health after sides are exchanged

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its two end letters, and these are the ones that trade places
exchanged means the letters at the two ends swap with one another

parts.note: salut is the French toast meaning good health

explanation.surface: A bone in good health after a change of sides.
explanation.walkthrough: Take SALUT, the French toast, and swap its first and last letters, S and T, as 'sides are exchanged' says.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle bone, which joins the leg to the foot, is a specific bone of the skeleton.

clue.text: Claim this novel method for stemming disappearance of rhino?

definitions.text: method for stemming disappearance of rhino?

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of claim this are made into something new

explanation.surface: A new way to stop rhinos vanishing, to save the species.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rhino' is old British slang for money, not the animal: a spending cap stems its disappearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap on spending prevents money draining away, and rhino is slang for money, so this method stops it vanishing.

clue.text: A group contributing to climate, but not me?

definitions.text: A group contributing to climate, but not me?

parts.words: A group contributing to climate, but not me?
parts.note: removing ME from climate leaves CL, I and AT, the chemical symbols for chlorine, iodine and astatine, members of one group of the periodic table

explanation.surface: An environmental group helps the climate cause, but the speaker opts out.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike ME from CLIMATE to leave CLIAT, then split it as Cl, I, At: three elements from group 17 of the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: Chlorine, iodine and astatine all belong to group 17 of the periodic table, the family that also includes fluorine and bromine.

clue.text: Whine when finally cutting retro jeans

indicators.note: the final letter cuts into the reversed brand, sitting inside it
retro means backwards here, so the brand is read in reverse

parts.note: Levis are a brand of jeans

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of when

explanation.surface: Someone moans when their old-fashioned jeans are finally cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retro' turns LEVIS into SIVEL; 'cutting' puts N inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To complain in a tearful, whining way is to whimper and moan, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Unnamed food stores stocking small cakes

indicators.note: the shortened stores stock the letter for small, holding it inside
N is the abbreviation for name, so unnamed drops that letter

parts.note: pantries are rooms or cupboards where food is stored

explanation.surface: Anonymous food shops are stocking little cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unnamed' takes N from PANTRIES to give PATRIES; 'stocking' puts S inside: PA-S-TRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet baked items such as tarts and Danishes are both, so cakes is a loose synonym.

clue.text: Material delivered by corrupt Senate

indicators.note: corrupt means the letters of the word Senate are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Goods handed over by a corrupt senate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges SENATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy cotton fabric woven like satin is a textile, so it is a kind of material.
